claims.text: An architecture test is a unit test that checks how the code is structured, such as which assemblies a project uses, instead of how it behaves.
At stage-2 Order.IdempotencyKey carries a comment saying a unique index guards it; the unique index is configured in DonHangDbContext (HasIndex(o => o.IdempotencyKey).IsUnique()).
EF Core has an attribute for declaring an index on an entity class ([Index] in namespace Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore), declared in the assembly Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Abstractions.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Indexes (data annotations, [Index] attribute); API reference IndexAttribute (assembly Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Abstractions)

claims.text: DomainReferencesNoOuterAssembly reads typeof(OrderService).Assembly.GetReferencedAssemblies(), keeps names starting with one of 7 prefixes (DonHang.Infrastructure, DonHang.Api, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore, Microsoft.AspNetCore, Npgsql, StackExchange.Redis, MailKit), then Assert.Empty.

Assembly.GetReferencedAssemblies returns the AssemblyName of every assembly the given assembly references; the compiler records a reference only for assemblies whose types the compiled code uses, so an unused PackageReference leaves no reference.
